How Pricing Works

Five compact steps build your commercial planning estimate.

Start with the operation and one useful sizing detail. Add only the goods, rhythm, ownership, and route facts that apply; each priced answer changes the estimate or resolves a named uncertainty.

01 | Operation & goods

What you clean matters as much as how much you clean.

Different goods require different cleaning, handling, and finishing. Choose the operation closest to yours so your planning range reflects how your laundry program actually works.

02 | Scale & weekly volume

Weekly volume determines the scale of your laundry program.

Share the number you know best, such as pounds, pieces, rooms, or another familiar measure. Shelton uses your selected goods to estimate weekly volume and plan the right production capacity and pickup schedule.

03 | Finish & return

Clean is only part of the service.

Pressing, hanging, folding, bundling, labeling, and protective packaging require different levels of labor and handling. They also determine how easily your team can put finished goods back into use.

    04 | Inventory ownership

    Who owns the goods changes how the program is structured.

    Customer-owned programs focus on cleaning, finishing, packaging, and return. Shelton-supplied programs also include inventory planning, replacements, and the working stock needed between service days. Many operations use a combination of both.

    Which description is closest to your operation?

    Supplied inventory tier

    Choose a planning quality tier. Exact goods, quantities, par, freight, setup, and customization are confirmed during Shelton review.

    There is no wrong starting point

    Many operations use a hybrid of owned and supplied goods. Shelton can help compare the models.

    05 | Location & route

    Your location and service schedule shape the route.

    Distance, traffic, building access, loading constraints, and pickup frequency all affect what dependable service requires. Share a ZIP code or address, then add any timing or access needs that apply to your operation.
